title: Discourse on the Dormition of the Holy Virgin

pairs.en: **The falling-asleep of our Lady the Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary, written by John, Archbishop of Thessalonica.**

To the wondrous, surpassingly glorious, and truly great Lady of the whole world, the ever-virgin Mother of our Saviour and God Jesus Christ, truly the Theotokos, a worthy hymn, honour, and glory are owed for ever by everything under heaven, because of the benefaction that came through her to all creation in the economy of the coming-in-the-flesh of the only-begotten Son and Word of God the Father.

After the voluntary suffering in the flesh, the resurrection from the dead, and the ascent into the heavens of the Word of God who for our sake was truly made flesh of her and became man, she remained with the holy apostles, spending no short time in the region of Judaea and Jerusalem, living for the most part in the house of the virgin and apostle whom the Lord loved, as the divine Scripture shows. [John 19:27] Then, when each of the apostles, at the command of the Holy Spirit, had set out to preach the gospel in all the world, after some time this all-glorious Virgin and Theotokos left the earth by a natural end.

sections.heading: Why Thessalonica had no feast of the Dormition

pairs.en: Now some did commit to writing the wonders that happened concerning her at that time, and almost everything under heaven keeps the yearly memory of her repose with festivity — except a few places, one of which is the region around this God-guarded metropolis of the Thessalonians. What then? Shall we condemn those before us for negligence or sloth? Far be it from us to say such a thing, or even to think it, seeing that they alone of all bequeathed to their homeland, as a matter of settled law, that exceptional glory: that we celebrate spiritually the memories not only of our local saints but of nearly all on earth who have contended for Christ, making ourselves God's own familiars by assemblies and prayers.

No — they were neither negligent nor slothful. But those who were present at the time wrote down, in love of the truth, as has been said, the account of her consummation; and afterwards certain malicious heretics threw in tares of their own and twisted what had been written. For this reason our fathers kept away from those writings, as being out of tune with the catholic Church, and from then on forgetfulness overtook the feast itself among them. And do not be astonished to hear that heretics corrupted writings, since they have been caught, at various times, doing the like to the epistles of the God-bearing Apostle and even to the holy Gospels themselves.

Yet we shall not, because of their God-hated treachery, spurn the documents of the truth. Rather, purging out the wicked over-sowing, we shall embrace what was truly done for the glory of God among his saints, and keep it in memory in a way that profits souls and pleases God. For this is just what we have found done both by those who went shortly before us and by the holy fathers long before them: the former with the so-called Travels of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, Andrew and John; the latter with most of the writings about the Christ-bearing martyrs. For one must truly clear the stones out of the road, as it is written, so that the flock God has chosen may not stumble. [Jeremiah 50:26]

sections.heading: The preacher's promise: only what truly happened

pairs.en: Since, then, it is altogether necessary — so that this Christ-loving metropolis may lack nothing good — that the benefactress and Lady of the world, the ever-virgin Theotokos Mary, be glorified in all sincerity, as we keep with spiritual gladness the memory of her repose so befitting God, we have rightly taken no small pains to set before your God-loving ears, for the rousing and building-up of souls, not everything we found written about her in different ways in different books, but only those things which are recorded as truly done and truly come to pass, and which are witnessed by the very places to this day. These we have gathered with the fear of God and the love of truth, giving no weight to the idle matter thrust in by the malice of those who falsified the accounts.

Hearing, then, with soul-profiting compunction the truly awesome and great wonders — wonders truly worthy of the Mother of God — that took place at her God-befitting repose, let us offer to the immaculate Lady and Theotokos Mary our thanksgiving, after God, and the glory that is her due, showing ourselves worthy of her gifts by good works. And you, receiving this small token of our love, and approving the unwearied zeal for better things to which the present writing exhorts you, repay the affection, as brothers and beloved children in the Lord, by earnest prayer, procuring for me always the help that comes from God; for his is the glory and the honour and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

sections.heading: An angel brings a palm from paradise

pairs.en: When the holy Theotokos Mary was about to lay aside the body, the great angel came to her and said: “Mary, rise; take this palm, which he who planted paradise gave me, and hand it to the apostles, so that holding it they may sing hymns before you; for after three days you lay aside the body. Behold, I am sending all the apostles to you, and they will tend your burial and behold your glory, until they carry you to your place.”

And Mary answered the angel: “Why have you brought this one palm only, and not one for each of them — lest it be given to one and the others murmur? And what is it you wish me to do? And what is your name, so that I can tell them if they ask?”

The angel said to her: “Why do you seek my name? It is a wonder past hearing. And do not be anxious about the palm, for through it many will be healed, and it will be a test for everyone in Jerusalem: to the one who believes it is revealed; from the one who does not believe it is hidden. Go, then, to the mountain.”

Then Mary went and climbed the Mount of Olives, the angel's light shining before her, the palm in her hand. And when she came to the mountain, the whole mountain rejoiced together with the plants that grew on it, so that the plants bowed their heads and worshipped. Seeing this, Mary was shaken, thinking that it was Jesus, and said: “Are you not the Lord? For so great a power has come with you that all these great plants have worshipped you. I tell you, no one works such power except the Lord of glory, who entrusted himself to me.”

Then the angel said to her: “No one can work signs except by his hands, for he gives power to everything that exists. I am he who receives the souls of those who humble themselves before God, and I carry them to the place of the just on the day they come out of the body. As for you — when you lay aside the body, I myself will come for you.”

Mary said to him: “My lord, in what form do you come to your elect? Tell me what will happen, so that I may do my part when you come to take me up.” And he said to her: “What is there to fear, Lady? When God sends for you, I shall not come alone: all the armies of the angels will come, and they will sing before you. Only hold the palm.” And when he had said this to her, the angel became as light and went up into heaven.

sections.heading: Mary's prayer in the inner chamber

pairs.en: Mary returned to her house, and at once the building shook because of the glory of the palm in her hand. After the shaking she went into her hidden inner room and laid the palm away in a linen cloth. Then she prayed to the Lord, saying: “Hear, Master, the prayer of your mother Mary who cries to you, and send your good pleasure upon me. Let no power come before my face in that hour when I go out of the body; but fulfil what you said to me when I wept before you and asked, 'What shall I do to pass by the powers that will come upon my soul?' For you promised me, saying: 'Do not weep. Neither angels are coming for you, nor archangels, nor cherubim, nor seraphim, nor any other power: I myself am coming for your soul.' Now, then, the pang has drawn near, as to a woman in travail.” And she prayed, saying: “I bless the everlasting light in which you dwell; I bless every planting of your hands, which abides for ever. Holy One, who dwell among the holy ones, hear the voice of my petition.” [Psalm 28:2]

sections.heading: Two angels come for every soul

pairs.en: When she had said this, she went out and said to the maidservant of her house: “Listen — go and call my kinsfolk and those who know me, and say, 'Mary is calling you.'” Her maidservant went and called them all, as she had been told. And when they had come in, Mary said to them: “Fathers and brothers, help me. I am about to go out of the body into my everlasting rest. Rise, then, and do me one great kindness. I ask no gold of you, and no silver — all such things are vain and perishable. I ask you a kindness: stay with me these two nights, and let each of you take a lamp and not let it go out for three days, and I will bless you before I depart.”

And they did as she said. And the report went round to all Mary's acquaintances and her kin, and they all gathered to her. Turning, Mary saw them all standing round her, and she lifted up her voice and said: “Fathers and brothers, let us help one another. Let us light our lamps and keep watch, for we do not know at what hour the thief is coming. [Matthew 24:43] It has been made known to me, my brothers, when I go out. I have learned it, I have been taught, and I am not afraid — for it is the common lot of all. Only one thing I fear: the warrior who makes war on everyone. Against the just and the faithful he can do nothing; but he prevails over the unbelieving, over sinners, and over all who do his will, and in them he does whatever he pleases. Over the just he does not prevail, because the angel of wickedness finds nothing of his own in them, and withdraws from them in shame.

“For two angels come to a man — one of justice and one of wickedness — and they arrive together with death. And when death begins to press upon the soul, the two angels come and examine the man's body. If he is found to have done the works of justice, the angel of justice rejoices over him, because the evil one has nothing in him; and then more angels come for that soul, singing hymns before it all the way to the place of all the just, while the angel of wickedness mourns, because he got no share in him. But if the man is found to have done wicked deeds, then that one rejoices, and takes with him other wicked spirits, and they seize the soul and drag it off, tearing at it; and the angel of justice grieves exceedingly. Now then, fathers and brothers, let us help one another, so that nothing evil may be found in us.”

As Mary was saying this, the women said to her: “Our sister, you who have become Mother of God and Lady of the whole world — if all of us are afraid, what have you to fear, you who are mother of the Lord? Woe to us — where are we to flee, if you speak like this? You are the expectation of us all. What shall we do, then, we who are least, and where shall we escape? If the shepherd fears the wolf, where shall the sheep run?”

Then all who stood round her began to weep. And Mary said to them: “Hush, my brothers, and do not weep, but glorify her who is now in your midst in this hour. I beg you: do not mourn the Virgin of God in this place — sing psalms instead of mourning, so that it may pass to all the generations of the earth and to every man of God. Sing psalms instead of lamenting, so that instead of lamentation it may become a blessing for you.”

sections.heading: John, the beloved disciple, arrives first

pairs.en: Having said this, Mary called all who were nearest her and said to them: “Rise, and pray.” And when they had prayed, they sat down and talked with one another of the mighty works of God and the signs he had done. And while they were talking, John the apostle arrived and knocked at Mary's door, opened it, and came in. When Mary saw him her spirit was shaken; she groaned, wept, and cried out with a loud voice: “John, my child, do not forget the word your Teacher commanded you concerning me, when I wept for him at the cross and said, 'You are going away, my Son — with whom do you leave me? With whom shall I make my home?' And he said to me, while you stood there listening: 'John is the one who will look after you.' Now then, child, do not forget what was commanded you for my sake. Remember that he loved you more than all the apostles. Remember that you, more than the others, lay upon his breast. Remember that to you alone, as you lay on his breast, he spoke the mystery which no one knows except me and you — because you are the virgin, and his chosen one — and he would not grieve me, since I had become his dwelling. For I said to him, 'Tell me what you have said to John'; and he gave you the charge, and you shared it with me. Now then, John my child, do not forsake me.”

As she said this, Mary wept with a quiet voice. And John could not bear it: his spirit was troubled, and he did not yet grasp what she was telling him, for he did not know that she was about to go out of the body. Then he said to her: “Mary, mother of the Lord, what do you want me to do for you? I left you my servant to bring you your food. Surely you would not have me transgress the command of my Lord, which he laid upon me when he said, 'Go about the whole world, until sin is destroyed'? Only tell me now the trouble of your soul: is there anything you lack?”

And Mary said to him: “John, my child, I need nothing of this world. But since the day after tomorrow I go out of the body, I beg you — do me a kindness. Keep my body safe, and lay it, by itself, in a tomb; and guard it, together with your brothers the apostles, because of the chief priests. For with my own ears I heard them saying: 'If we find her body, we will give it to the fire, because from her came forth that deceiver.'”

When John heard her say, “I am going out of the body,” he fell on his knees and wept, saying: “O Lord, who are we, that you have shown us these tribulations? We have not yet forgotten the first ones, and behold, we must endure yet another affliction. Why do I not go out of the body instead, and let you watch over me, O Mary?”

Hearing John speak so and weep, Mary begged those standing by to be quiet — for they too were weeping — and she checked John, saying: “Child, bear with me patiently, and leave off your weeping.” Then John rose and wiped away his tears. And Mary said to him: “Come out with me, and ask the crowd to sing psalms while I speak with you.” And while they sang, she brought John into her inner room and showed him her funeral clothes and everything prepared for her body, saying: “John, my child, you know that I have nothing on earth except my grave-clothes and two tunics. There are two widows here: when I go out of the body, give one to each of them.”

After this she led him to where the palm was that the angel had given her, and said to him: “John, my child, take this palm, so that you may carry it before my bier; for so it was told me.” But he said to her: “I cannot take it without my fellow apostles, since they are not here — lest, when they come, there be murmuring and complaint among us. For there is one among them greater than I, who has been set over us. But if we come together on it, there will be good agreement.”

And just as they came out of the inner room, there was a great clap of thunder, so that all in the place were shaken. And after the sound of the thunder, the apostles came down on clouds at Mary's door — eleven of them, each seated on a cloud: first Peter, second Paul, he too borne on a cloud and numbered with the apostles, for he had the beginning of faith in Christ. After them the rest of the apostles also gathered on clouds at Mary's door. And they greeted one another, gazing at each other and marvelling at how they had come together in one place. And Peter said: “Brothers, let us pray to God who has gathered us — above all because our brother Paul is with us.” When Peter had said this, they stood in prayer and lifted up one voice: “Let us pray that it may be made known to us why God has brought us together.” Then each yielded the honour of leading the prayer to another.

So Peter said to Paul: “Paul, my brother, rise and pray before me; for I have rejoiced with joy unspeakable that you have come to the faith of Christ.” And Paul said to him: “Forgive me, father Peter — I am a newly-planted convert, not worthy even to follow in the prints of your feet. How should I pray before you? You are the pillar of light, and all these brothers standing round are better men than I. You, then, father, pray for me and for all, that the grace of the Lord may remain with us.”

Then the apostles rejoiced at Paul's humility and said: “Father Peter, it is you who were set over us: pray before us.” And Peter prayed, saying: “God and our Father — and the Lord Jesus Christ will glorify you, as the ministry that is in me is glorified; for I am the least of the brothers, and a servant. As I was chosen, so also were you, and one is the calling that has come to us all. So whoever glorifies another glorifies Jesus, and not a man; for this is the commandment of the Teacher, that we love one another.” [John 15:12]

Then Peter, stretching out his hands, gave thanks, saying: “Master almighty, who sit upon the cherubim on high [2 Kings 19:15] and look upon the lowly, [Psalm 113:6] who dwell in unapproachable light [1 Timothy 6:16] — you loose what is hard-bound; [Daniel 5:12] you uncover hidden treasures; [Isaiah 45:3] you have planted your kindness in us. What god is there so ready to be gracious as you? You have not withdrawn your love for mankind from us, for you save from every evil all who hope in you [2 Maccabees 6:16] — you who live and have conquered death, from now and unto the ages of ages. Amen.” And they greeted one another once more.

sections.heading: "Bless me too": the apostles greet Mary

pairs.en: And at once John came into their midst and said: “Bless me too, all of you.” Then they embraced him as well, each according to his own rank. And after the greeting Peter said to him: “John, beloved of the Lord, how did you come here, and how many days have you been here?” And John said: “It happened while I was in the city of Sardis, teaching until the ninth hour: a cloud came down upon the place where we were gathered, snatched me up in the sight of all who were with me, and carried me all the way here. I knocked at the door, they opened to me, and I found a crowd around our mother Mary; and she said to me, 'I am going out of the body.' I could not bear it there in the midst of those standing round her, and grief weighed me down. Now, brothers, when you go in to her at dawn, do not weep and do not be troubled — lest the crowds around her see us weeping and begin to waver about the resurrection, and say, 'So even they were afraid of death.' Rather, let us take heart from the words of the good Teacher.”

Then the apostles, going into Mary's house at dawn, said with one voice: “Blessed Mary, mother of all who are being saved, grace be with you.” And Mary said to them: “How did you come in here? Who told you that I am going out of the body? And how did you gather here? For I see you assembled together, and I am glad.” And each told the country from which he had been carried off, and that “snatched up on clouds, we were gathered here.” Then they all glorified her, saying: “May the Lord who saves all bless you.”

And Mary rejoiced in spirit and said: “I bless you, the giver of every blessing. I bless the dwelling-place of your glory. I bless you, giver of the light, who made your sojourn in my womb. I bless all the works of your hands, which obey you in all subjection. I bless you, who have blessed us. I bless the words of life that came from your mouth and were given to us in truth. For I believe that what you have said is coming to pass for me. You said, 'I will send all the apostles to you when you go out of the body' — and behold, they are gathered, and I am in their midst like a fruitful vine, as in the time when I was with you. I bless you with every blessing. Let the rest of what you told me come to pass as well; for you said, 'You shall see me when you go out of the body.'”

When she had said this, she called Peter and all the apostles and brought them into her inner room and showed them her funeral clothes. And after this she went out and sat in the midst of them all, the lamps burning; for they did not let them go out, as Mary had commanded.

sections.heading: Peter's night sermon: the lamp of the inner man

pairs.en: Now when the sun had set, on the second day before her going out of the body, Peter said to all the apostles: “Brothers, let whoever has a word of instruction speak it, exhorting the crowd through the whole night.” And the apostles said to him: “And who is wiser than you? We shall be glad above all to hear your instruction.”

Then Peter began to speak: “Brothers, and all of you who have come to this place at this hour of the departure of our mother Mary: you have done well to light lamps that shine with the fire of this visible earth. But I want each of you also to take up his lamp in the unending age — the lamp that needs no fuel: the three-wicked lamp of the inner man, which is our body and soul and spirit. If these three shine with the true fire, the fire you are striving toward, you will not be put to shame when you enter the wedding to rest with the Bridegroom. So it is with our mother Mary. The light of her lamp has filled the whole world, and it will not be quenched until the consummation of the age, so that all who wish to be saved may take courage from her. Do not think, then, that Mary's death is death. It is not death but everlasting life, because the death of the just is glorified in the presence of God. [Psalm 116:15] This is glory — and the second death will have no power to trouble them.”

While Peter was still speaking, a great light shone in the house among them all, so that the light of their own lamps grew dim; and a voice came, saying: “Peter, speak to them with knowledge, as much as they can bear. For the best physician suits the cure to the sufferings of the sick, and the nurse gives the nourishment that fits the child's age.”
And Peter lifted up his voice and said: “We bless you, O Christ, the helm of our souls.”

sections.heading: The parable of the two banished servants

pairs.en: Then Peter said to the virgins who were there: “Hear what your grace is, and your glory, and your honour. Blessed are all who keep the garment of their holiness. Hear and learn what our Teacher said to us: 'The kingdom of heaven,' he says, 'is like virgins.' [Matthew 25:1] He did not say, 'It is like many years,' because years pass away, but the name of virginity will not pass away. He did not liken it to a rich man, because riches dwindle, but the name of virginity remains. Therefore I believe that you will be in glory. This is why he likened the kingdom of heaven to you: because you are free of care. When death is sent upon you, you do not say, 'Woe to us — where are we going, leaving behind our poor children, or our great riches, or our planted fields, or our great estates?' You care for none of these things. You have no anxiety at all except for your virginity; and when death is sent upon you, you are found ready, lacking nothing. And so that you may learn that nothing is greater than the name of virtue, and nothing heavier than the things of this world, take this in too.

“There was a rich man in a certain city, with abundance of every kind, and he had house-servants. And it happened that two of his servants sinned against him, disobeying his words. Their master, angered, banished them to a distant country for a set time, intending to call them back afterwards. One of the banished servants built himself a house, planted a vineyard, set up a bakehouse, and got himself other great possessions. But the other servant put by in gold whatever his labour earned him; and calling a goldsmith, he had a crown made, saying to the goldsmith: 'I am a servant; I have a master, and he has a son. Figure them upon the golden crown.' The goldsmith did his craft and said to the servant: 'Rise, and set the crown upon your head.' But the servant said: 'Take your wage; I have my own proper time for wearing the crown.' Then the goldsmith understood what the servant meant, and went off to his own house.

“After this, the appointed term of the banishment drew near, and the master sent a certain stern officer to them, telling him: 'Unless you present them to me within seven days, you are in peril.' The man who was sent set out with great haste, and coming to that country he sought the servants by night and by day. And laying hold of the one who had acquired the house and the vineyard and the other property, he said to him: 'Come, let us go; my master has sent me for you.' And the man made as if to answer, 'Let us go' — but then said to him: 'Bear with me until I have sold all the goods I acquired here.' Then the officer said to him: 'I cannot delay. My appointed term is seven days, and fearing my master's threat, I cannot wait.' Then the servant wept and said: 'Woe is me, for I have been found unready.' And the officer said to him: 'O worst of servants — did you not know your own servitude? Did you not know that you were banished, and that whenever the master wills, he sends for you? Why did you plant vineyards, from which you can carry nothing away, and let yourself be found unready? Before I came for you, you ought to have made yourself ready.' Then, weeping, the servant said: 'Woe is me! I thought I should remain in banishment for ever; I did not believe that my master would send to seek me, and that is why I got myself all this property in this land.' Then the officer drove him out, carrying nothing at all with him.

“But when the other servant heard that a man had been sent for them, he rose, took up the crown, went to the road by which the officer was to pass, and waited steadily. And when he came, the servant said to him: 'My master has sent you for me. Let us go together with joy — nothing holds me back, and even what I own is light. I have nothing else at all but this crown of gold. I made it while I waited and prayed every day that my lord might be gracious to me, and that my master would send for me and take me out of this banishment — before any should envy me and take the crown from me. Now I have obtained my prayer. Rise, then; let us go.'

“So the two servants set off with the officer. And when their master saw them, he said to the one who had nothing: 'Where is the work of all that long time of your banishment?' And the servant answered: 'Master, you sent me a stern soldier, and I begged him to let me sell my goods and carry them in my hands; and he told me, ”I have no leave for that.”' Then his master said to him: 'O wicked servant — now you remembered to sell, when I had already sent for you. Why did you not keep your banishment before your eyes, and reckon that all that abundance was nothing to you?' And in anger he ordered him bound hand and foot and sent away to other, harsher places. But calling the servant who carried the crown, he said to him: 'Well done, good and faithful servant. You longed for freedom — the crown you made shows it, for the crown belongs to the free. Yet you did not dare to wear it without your master's leave, for a servant cannot be set free except by his own master. As you desired freedom, then, receive it from me.' Then he is given his freedom, and is set over many things.”

sections.heading: We are all in exile: Peter to the crowd

pairs.en: When Peter had said this to the virgins who surrounded Mary, he turned to the crowd and said: “Let us also hear, brothers, what is coming upon us. For truly we — the race of men — are the virgins of the true Bridegroom, the Son of God, the Father of all creation. God, angered with our race at the beginning, cast Adam out into this world; and so we live in it as people under displeasure, as it were in banishment. And we are not permitted to remain in it: each one's day comes, and he will be removed to where our fathers and forefathers are — where Abraham is, and Isaac, and Jacob. For when each man's consummation arrives, the stern officer — that is, death — is sent to him. And when death comes upon the soul of a sinner lying sick, a man who has heaped up for himself many sins and iniquities, and presses him hard, then the man pleads, saying: 'Bear with me this once, until I redeem the sins I planted in my own body.' But death does not consent — for how can he yield, when the man's appointed term is already fulfilled? So, having nothing of justice, the man is carried off to the place of torment.

“But if a man has done the works of justice, he rejoices and says: 'Nothing holds me back; I have nothing to carry with me now except the name of virtue.' And he entreats death, saying: 'Do not leave me in this land, lest some envy me and take from me the name of my virginity.' Then the soul goes out of the body and is borne with hymns to the immortal Bridegroom, who sets it in the place of rest. Now then, brothers, strive like men, knowing that we do not remain here for ever.”

sections.heading: The Lord comes for his mother's soul

pairs.en: While Peter was saying these things, strengthening the crowds until daybreak, the sun rose. And Mary rose and went outside, and lifting up her hands she prayed to the Lord. After the prayer she went in and lay down upon her bed. Peter sat at her head, John at her feet, and the rest of the apostles in a circle around her bed. And about the third hour of the day there came a great thunder out of heaven, and a fragrance of sweetness, so that sleep overcame all who stood around, except only the apostles and three virgins, whom the Lord kept awake so that they might bear witness to Mary's funeral rites and to her glory.

And behold, the Lord arrived upon the clouds with a multitude of angels beyond number. And Jesus himself, with Michael, entered the chamber where Mary was, while the angels sang hymns and stood outside the chamber. And the moment the Saviour entered, he found the apostles around holy Mary, and he greeted them all; and after that he greeted his own mother. And Mary opened her mouth and blessed him, saying: “I bless you, because you have not grieved me in anything you promised. For you promised that you would not permit angels to come for my soul, but that you would come for it yourself. And it has happened to me, Lord, according to your word. Who am I, the lowly one, that I have been counted worthy of such glory?” And as she said this, she brought her stewardship to its fulfilment, her face turned toward the Lord with a gentle smile. And the Lord, receiving her soul, placed it in the hands of Michael, after wrapping it in veils whose splendour no words can tell.

And we, the apostles, beheld the soul of Mary as it was given into Michael's hands: complete with every member of a human being, except only the form of female and male, with nothing else in it but the likeness of the whole body, and a whiteness seven times brighter than the sun. And Peter, filled with joy, asked the Lord: “Which of us, then, has a soul as white as Mary's?” The Lord said to him: “O Peter, the souls of all who are born into this world are like this; but when they go out of the body, they are not found so white, because they were sent into the world one way and are found another — for they loved the darkness of many sins. But if a man guards himself from the iniquities of the darkness of this age, and so goes out of the body, his soul is found white like this.”

Then again the Saviour said to Peter: “Guard the body of Mary, my dwelling-place, with care. Go out on the left side of the city, and you will find a new tomb. Lay the body in it, and remain there, as she commanded you.”

While the Saviour was saying this, the body of the holy Theotokos itself cried out before them all, saying: “Remember me, King of glory! Remember me, for I am your own handiwork. Remember me, for I guarded the treasure that was entrusted to me.” Then Jesus said to the body: “I will not abandon you, treasure-house of my pearl. I will not abandon you, who were found a faithful keeper of the deposit entrusted to you. Far be it from me to abandon you — the ark who steered her own Steersman. Far be it from me to abandon you — the treasure kept under seal until it should be sought.” And saying this, the Saviour became invisible.

sections.heading: The procession and the high priest's hands

pairs.en: Then Peter and the other apostles and the three virgins prepared Mary's body for burial and laid it on the bier. And after this, those who had been overcome by sleep awoke. Peter brought out the palm and said to John: “You are the virgin; it is you who ought to sing before the bier, holding it.” And John said to him: “You are our father and bishop; it is you who ought to go before the bed, until we carry it to the place.” And Peter said to him: “So that none of us may be grieved, let us crown the bier with it.”

Then the apostles rose and lifted Mary's bed. And Peter struck up the hymn, singing: “Israel went out of Egypt — alleluia!” [Psalm 114:1] And the Lord and the angels were upon the clouds, going along unseen, singing and blessing; only the voice of the angels was heard. And the sound of a great multitude went out over all Jerusalem; and the chief priests, hearing the tumult and the voice of the singers, were troubled and said: “What is this tumult?” And someone told them: “Mary has gone out of the body, and the apostles are singing hymns around her.” And immediately Satan entered into them, and filled with rage they said: “Come, let us go out and kill the apostles, and burn the body that carried that sorcerer.” And rising up, they went out with swords and weapons to kill them. And at once the angels who were upon the clouds struck them with blindness, and they went dashing their heads against the walls, unable to see where they were going — all except one chief priest alone, who had found the way out, so as to see what was happening.

When he drew near the apostles and saw the bier crowned and the apostles singing, he was filled with a great fury and said: “See what fearful glory the dwelling of the one who plundered our nation now enjoys!” And in a great fury he rushed at the bier, and meaning to overturn it, he seized it at the place where the palm was, and pulling, tried to drag it to the ground. And instantly his hands stuck fast to the bier and were severed at the elbows, and hung there upon the bier.

Then the man wept before all the apostles, begging them: “Do not abandon me in so great a strait.” And Peter said to him: “The power to help you is not mine, nor any of these men's. But if you believe that Jesus is the Son of God — the one you all rose against, and seized, and killed — then you shall be released from this exemplary punishment.” And the man said: “Did we not know that he is the Son of God? But what could we do, when the love of money was darkening our eyes? For our fathers, when they were about to die, called us to them and said: 'Children, behold, God has chosen you out of all the tribes, to stand before this people in power, and not to labour in the material things of this earth. This is your work: to build up this people, and to receive from them all tithes and first-fruits and every firstborn that opens the womb. But take care, children, lest the place grow rich beyond measure through your doing, and you turn to trading for yourselves, and provoke God to anger. Rather, give your surplus to the poor and the orphans and the widows of your people, and do not overlook a soul in affliction.' But we did not listen to the traditions of our fathers. Seeing that the place had grown exceedingly rich, we set out the firstborn of the sheep and the oxen and all the beasts on the tables of the money-changers, for buying and selling. And when the Son of God came, he cast them all out of the place, money-changers and all, saying: 'Take these things away — do not make my Father's house a house of trade.' [John 2:16] But we, with our eyes on the customs of ours that he had annulled, plotted evil in our hearts, and rose against him and killed him, knowing full well that he is the Son of God. Do not hold our malice against us, but forgive me; for this has happened to me because God loves me — so that I may live.”

Then Peter had the bier set down, and said to the chief priest: “If you now believe with your whole heart, go and kiss the body of Mary, and say: 'I believe in you, and in the God who was born of you.'” Then the chief priest blessed holy Mary in the Hebrew tongue for three hours, and would let no one touch her, bringing forward testimonies from the holy books of Moses and of the rest of the prophets — that it is written of her that she would become the temple of the God of glory — so that all who heard marvelled at such traditions, which they had never heard before. And Peter said to him: “Go, and join your hands to one another.” And he joined them, saying: “In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of Mary the Theotokos, let my hands be joined to each other.” And at once they became as they had been from the beginning, lacking nothing.

And Peter said to him: “Rise, take a leaf from the palm, and go into the city. You will find a blinded crowd unable to find the way out; tell them what has happened to you, and lay this leaf on the eyes of whoever believes, and at once he will see again.”

And the chief priest went, as Peter had commanded him, and found many blind men — these were the ones the angels had struck with blindness — weeping and saying: “Woe to us! What was done in Sodom has come upon us too. For first God struck them with blindness, and after that he brought fire from heaven and burned them. Woe to us — behold, we are already maimed; next comes the fire!” Then the man with the palm-leaf spoke to them about faith. And whoever believed received his sight; and whoever did not believe did not see again, but remained blind.

sections.heading: The empty tomb and the blessing

pairs.en: Then the apostles, carrying the precious body of our most glorious Lady, the Theotokos and ever-virgin Mary, laid it in a new tomb, where the Saviour had shown them. And they remained there with one accord, keeping watch, for three days. And after the third day they opened the coffin to venerate the precious tabernacle of her who is worthy of all praise — and we found only the grave-wrappings; for she had been taken away by Christ God, who was made flesh of her, to the everlasting inheritance.

And our Lord Jesus Christ himself, who glorified his immaculate mother, the Theotokos Mary — he will glorify those who glorify her. Those who keep her yearly memory he will save out of every danger, and he will fill their houses with good things, as he filled the house of Onesiphorus; [2 Timothy 1:16] and they shall receive forgiveness of sins both here and in the age to come. For he showed her to be his cherubic throne upon earth, a heaven on earth, the hope and refuge and confidence of our race — so that, keeping mystically the feast of her divine falling-asleep, we may find mercy and grace in this present age and in the age to come, by the grace and love for mankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and might, with his Father who is without beginning and the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

sections.heading: Another ending: the apostle who came late

pairs.en: *(The ending as the Venice manuscript tells it.)*

Then the apostles, carrying the bed, brought her to the tomb; and having laid her there, they remained on the spot three days, guarding her with unceasing psalms and hymns. But by God's dispensation one of the apostles was not present at the funeral of the Mother of God; and he came after the third day to Gethsemane, and mourned very bitterly that he had not been counted worthy to look upon the most holy Theotokos, who is wider than the heavens. The apostles resolved to open the tomb, so that he too might be counted worthy to see the Mother of God. But when they opened it and looked in, they found the tomb empty, and the body of the Mother of God was not in it; and they understood that it had been translated by the godlike angels to paradise.

This is the falling-asleep of Mary the blessed, the mother of the Lord. And our Lord Jesus Christ himself, who glorified his immaculate mother, the Theotokos and Virgin — he glorifies in return those who glorify her, and magnifies those who magnify her, not only in this age but also in the age to come, and leads them into his heavenly kingdom; for to him belongs all glory, honour, and worship, with his Father who is without beginning and his all-holy, good, and life-giving Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
